reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Ps 118 is an identity psalm (WEB=MT, 29 verses, no title -- web_mt_offset_map.json), so no dual-cite is required and the row's plain web: refs are correctly formed; citation_sweep.py is clean on the whole cluster. The refrain clause is byte-identical (collate.py) at Ps.118.1, 118.2, 118.3, and 118.4 -- the row's 'across all 4 verses' claim holds exactly, 4/4. The verse-initial hodu count (2 verses: 118.1 and 118.29) is independently confirmed by a skeleton sweep restricted to Ps 118 -- no third occurrence exists anywhere in the psalm, and the inclusio's other half (v29) is literally byte-for-byte identical to v1 (direct string equality against verse_map_oshb.json, not just a collate substring match). Grouping vv1-4 as 'refrain_unit' rather than 'strophe' is a defensible, non-idiosyncratic use of the controlled vocabulary: unlike every other row in this cluster (which uses 'strophe' for movements that CONTAIN a refrain among other material -- e.g. the tripled-refrain-plus-resolution at vv10-14, the doubled-acclamation-plus-testimony at vv15-18), vv1-4 is nothing but the refrain: v1 states the clause once, vv2-4 are three parallel calls supplying only that same clause restated for each addressee. check_tiling.py confirms this row opens the cluster's exact, gapless tiling of Ps.118.1-29. 'High' confidence is well-supported by the strength of the byte-level corroboration on every load-bearing claim.

Re-derived independently. The doubled proverb's shared opening (Ps.118.8) is byte-identical (collate.py) to Ps.118.9's opening; the two verses diverge only at the final word, confirmed as two distinct forms -- exactly as the row states, no more and no less. The distress/spacious-place wordplay at 118.5 collates at byte tier for the whole verse. check_refs_mirror.py and check_universals.py are both clean on this row -- no unmirrored prose ranges, no unswept absolute claims. The rejected_alternative identifies a real (if not compelling) alternative seam -- splitting the confidence declaration (vv6-7) from the doubled proverb (vv8-9) -- and gives one adequate sentence against it; no second sentence is owed since no rival disclosure is mandated here. 'High' confidence is reasonable: this is one of the cluster's cleaner, most tightly-corroborated thematic movements.

Re-derived independently against ground-truth verse text (Ps.118.10-14). The row's headline claims check out: the closing clause is byte-identical (collate.py) across all three of 118.10-12, and the adversative turn at v13 ('pushed back... but Yahweh helped') genuinely answers the threat just described, supporting a strophe (not refrain_unit) call -- consistent with this cluster's own vocabulary discipline (contrast 393). But observed_substrate_signals[1] misidentifies its own evidence: it labels the phrase tagged oshb:Ps.118.10 as 'a long [spelled form of the surround verb]', but that phrase is not a form of the surround verb (סבב) at all -- it is the SAME closing refrain clause already correctly quoted earlier in this row's own rationale, misattributed here as verb-form evidence. The row's underlying numeric claim (4 occurrences of the surround verb, 2 spellings, distributed v10 / v11 x2 / v12) is independently correct from the ground-truth text -- but the specific Hebrew string offered as evidence for the 'long' spelling is the wrong string. 'Medium' confidence is appropriately cautious for a row that turns out to carry a citation defect.

challenges.claim: The Hebrew cited as the 'long spelled form' of the surround verb (tagged oshb:Ps.118.10) is not a form of the surround verb at all -- it is the row's own closing refrain clause, misattributed as verb-form evidence.
challenges.evidence: Ground truth Ps.118.10 (verse_map_oshb.json): "כָּל גּוֹיִ֥ם סְבָב֑וּנִי בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם". The true long spelling of the surround verb is the verse's third word, "סְבָב֑וּנִי" (byte-collated, collate.py, present in 118.10 and, at accent_stripped tier, in the second half of 118.11). The string the row actually cites as the 'long form' -- "בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם" -- is instead the closing clause that recurs byte-identical (collate.py) at the end of 118.10, 118.11, AND 118.12, and is already correctly named as the refrain elsewhere in this same row's rationale. The row's count (4 occurrences, 2 spellings) is independently correct; only this one parenthetical citation names the wrong string.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. The doubled right-hand acclamation is byte-identical (collate.py) between Ps.118.15 and 118.16. The WEB quotation-mark claim is confirmed precisely against verse_map_web.json: v15's text opens an unclosed curly quote before 'The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly,' and v16 closes it after the repeated line -- exactly the 'opens at v15, carried through v16' pattern the row describes, nothing more, nothing less. check_refs_mirror.py and check_universals.py are both clean on this row. The voice distinction (quoted communal acclamation vv15-16 vs first-person testimony vv17-18) is a genuine, well-evidenced literary seam. 'Medium' confidence is reasonably calibrated -- the row itself flags ending at v16 as 'possible', an honest hedge.

Re-derived independently. The gate-root exclusivity claim is confirmed by an all-29-verse skeleton sweep of Ps 118: the root underlying both 'gates of righteousness' (v19) and 'the gate' (v20) occurs ONLY at 118.19 and 118.20 in this psalm -- the row's '2 gate references, both inside this row' holds exactly. The three-way voice shift (2nd-person imperative plea v19 -> 3rd-person declarative reply v20 -> 1st-person resumed testimony v21) is confirmed from the Hebrew grammar of each verse. Two independent, tool-confirmed defects nonetheless stand: (1) check_refs_mirror.py flags this row -- the rejected_alternative argues 'no addressee inside vv14-18' in prose, naming that whole range, but boundary_evidence_refs mirrors only 118.18 of it; 118.14-17 are argued but uncited, a real completeness gap under the campaign's own MUST-mirror rule. (2) check_universals.py flags the same clause as an unswept absence claim carrying no digit-bearing count. Separately: this row claims 'high' confidence for exactly the seam the book strategy's own §7 names as an expected low-confidence region ('118's antiphonal structure'), and the row's own rejected_alternative concedes the alternative reading is 'possible' -- a high-confidence label sits uneasily next to an acknowledged live alternative in a region the strategy itself flags for caution, even though the underlying seam argument is sound on the merits.

The plea/acclamation voice distinction is confirmed from the Hebrew (2nd-person vocative-imperative at v25 vs 3rd-person passive-participle declarative at v26, matching WEB's own rendering). check_refs_mirror.py is clean on this row -- no unmirrored prose ranges. One minor observation, not filed as a formal challenge: check_universals.py flags this row's rejected_alternative ('...with no independent speaker change marking a seam inside it') as an unswept absence claim; on inspection the underlying claim is true (no explicit second speaker is introduced within vv25-27), and the row already carries 'medium' confidence with an honest hedge about which party speaks which line ('without settling which party (priests, pilgrims) speaks which'). This reads as a minor register nit rather than a material evidence defect -- support stands.
